speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain and difficulty in hand movement; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse? Did this injury happen suddenly after a trauma, or did it develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (with a history of possible distal radius fracture). The location of pain in the thumb and wrist, exacerbated by holding an infant, is classic for de Quervain's tenosynovitis. I will proceed with a physical exam maneuver to confirm this and rule out a chronic fracture from your fall.
